description: We're not here to take part, we're here to take over.
summary:
Earth's closest parallels to every part of a Moon or Mars base.

Our NASA Space Apps 2026 entry for Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars. Event: 14–15 November 2026.

No single place on Earth can stand in for a Moon or Mars base. So we split base-building into challenges, and for each one we rank the Earth sites best suited to test it. Every match shows what is similar, how similar, and where it breaks.
details:
Parallels
Earth's closest parallels to every part of a Moon or Mars base.

WHAT WE MADE
Parallels is a free website. It finds the places on Earth where teams can test each part of a Moon or Mars base.

No one place on Earth can copy a full base. Because of this, we divide a base into challenges, for example surface, resources, dryness, heat swing, shelter and dust. For each challenge, Parallels finds the places on Earth that are most similar to the base site.

HOW IT WORKS
We divide all land on Earth into 91,971 squares. Each square is approximately 50 km wide. We compare each square with 11 base sites:
- Moon (6): the south pole, four NASA Artemis III regions and the Shackleton rim.
- Mars (5): Jezero, Gale, Arcadia Planitia, Deuteronilus Mensae and the Arsia Mons caves.

For each square, we measure 17 traits, for example temperature, rain, slope, rock type and minerals. We rank each trait against all land on Earth. Then we combine the ranks into one score from 0 to 100.

On the website, you select a base site. The Finder shows the best 2% of land on a globe and a list of the 20 best places. Each place has one colour for each challenge: green shows "very close", red shows "far off". You can change the weight of each challenge, and the list changes immediately. Four presets are available: Balanced, Rover mobility, Life support and Habitat structure.

Each place has its own page. The page shows what is similar, how similar it is, and where the match stops. Each value shows the name of its dataset. If data is missing, the page shows that it is missing.

NEW PLACES
Teams use a small number of famous analog sites again and again, for example the Atacama Desert, Hawaii and Antarctica. Parallels marks the places that are more than 100 km from all 50 known analog sites in our list. By default, the list shows only these new places.

WHAT EARTH CANNOT COPY
Earth cannot copy low gravity, the vacuum of the Moon, the thin air of Mars or space radiation. Parallels shows these limits for each base site.

HOW WE CHECKED THE METHOD
Before each test, we recorded the rules in git. After each test, we published the result, pass or fail. Known analog sites must get higher scores than ordinary places, for example farms, forests and cities. On the test places that we kept separate, known analogs got the higher score 96% of the time for the Moon and 76% of the time for Mars. Of the 15 checks with sufficient sites, 10 pass. All results are on the website.

NASA DATA
NASA data does the main scoring work.
- Earth: NASA POWER climate, NASA EMIT minerals and MODIS land cover.
- Moon: LRO LOLA elevation, LRO Diviner temperatures, and the LOLA/PGDA sunlight and permanent shadow maps.
- Mars: Mars Odyssey GRS hydrogen, MGS TES dust cover, and the USGS HRSC-MOLA elevation map.
- Images: NASA Blue Marble and Landsat (through NASA GIBS), NASA Moon Trek, NASA Mars Trek, the NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit and the NASA Image and Video Library.
Partner and other data: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (ESA) for Earth terrain, the GLiM rock map and Natural Earth.

WHO CAN USE IT
Mission planners and test teams can use Parallels to find new test sites. Students can use the Learn page to learn about the Moon and Mars. The website is static. It has no server and no keys, so it continues to operate without maintenance.

HOW WE USED AI
The idea and the key design decisions are our team's. Claude (Anthropic) helped research the challenge, write our planning documents, and write and test the code and data pipeline. Our logo was drawn with AI. We check its work at each checkpoint.

Live site: https://parallelsbyrmd.vercel.app
